title: GRASP for change and variation
idea: Four GRASP rules handle change: Polymorphism replaces type switches, Pure Fabrication invents a non-domain class, Indirection adds a middleman, and Protected Variations hides unstable parts behind interfaces.
points: Polymorphism: when behaviour varies by type, give each type its own implementation.
Pure Fabrication: invent a non-domain class when no domain class should own a job.
Indirection: an intermediate object decouples two classes so either can change alone.
Protected Variations: find what will change and wrap it in a stable interface.

hero.title: One quote through four GRASP roles

steps.caption: The quote form needs a yearly premium. It knows only `QuoteService`, never a rule class.
Indirection: `QuoteService` sits between the form and the rules and validates the sum insured once.
Pure Fabrication: `RuleRegistry` is no real-world thing. It exists to map cover codes to rules.
Protected Variations: callers see only the `PremiumRule` interface. New covers do not ripple outward.
Polymorphism: Java dispatches to `PetRule.premiumCents`. No `switch` on the cover type exists anywhere.
The premium travels back to the form. Adding a cover means one new class and one registration.

code.title: The problem
code.caption: A `switch` on cover codes. A new cover is silently quoted at zero.

walk.text: The quote desk owns every cover's pricing, so each new cover edits this class.
Behaviour varies by type through a string `switch`. The compiler cannot check it is complete.
The new cover falls into `default` and returns zero. No error, just free insurance.
Look at the PET line in the output: a premium of zero went out unnoticed.

code.title: The fix
code.caption: Each GRASP rule has a visible home. Unknown covers fail loudly instead of pricing at zero.

walk.text: Protected Variations: pricing rules will keep changing, so they hide behind `PremiumRule`.
Polymorphism is the Strategy pattern from c08 seen as a placement rule: each cover owns its price.
Pure Fabrication: the registry is invented to own lookups. It rejects unknown covers.
Indirection: the form depends on `QuoteService` alone; rules can change behind it.
Main wires the parts once. `BOAT` is not registered, so it raises a clear error.

pitfalls: A `default` branch that returns zero hides missing cases; throw instead, or remove the switch.
Adding Indirection everywhere creates layers that only forward calls; add it where change is likely.
Pure Fabrications named `Helper` or `Manager` collect unrelated jobs; name them for one job.

quiz.q: `QuoteService` calls a credit bureau's client library directly. The bureau may change next year. Which GRASP rule fits?
options: Information Expert: let QuoteService score credit itself
Protected Variations: hide the bureau behind a CreditCheck interface
Creator: let QuoteService construct the bureau client
Controller: route credit calls through the UI controller
quiz.why: The bureau is a known point of change. A stable `CreditCheck` interface keeps `QuoteService` unaware of the library, so switching bureaus touches one adapter class.

takeaway: Find what varies, hide it behind an interface, and dispatch polymorphically.

starters: How is Protected Variations different from the Open/Closed Principle?
